overview: CenterPoint Energy is a pure-play, fully regulated public utility holding company whose subsidiaries own and operate electric transmission and distribution assets (Houston Electric in the ERCOT Gulf Coast region and SIGECO/Indiana Electric, a vertically integrated utility in southwestern Indiana) and natural gas local distribution systems in Texas, Minnesota, Indiana and (until an announced divestiture closes) Ohio. The company serves more than seven million metered electric and gas customers across four states and earns its income almost entirely through cost-of-service rate regulation rather than commodity or market exposure. CenterPoint is mid-execution on a $65.5-$70.7 billion 10-year (2026-2035) capital plan aimed at rate-base growth, grid resiliency and accommodating rapid electric load growth (data centers, industrial electrification) in the Houston service territory.

business_model.summary: Regulated "wires and pipes" utility that earns a regulator-approved return on capital invested in transmission, distribution and (in Indiana) generation assets; revenue is a function of rate base, approved ROE, and volumes delivered (with several tracker/true-up mechanisms that dampen commodity and weather risk). No Registrant makes direct retail commodity sales of electricity; REPs and gas-cost pass-throughs insulate margins from fuel price swings.

revenue_streams.name: Electric (Houston Electric T&D + Indiana Electric T&D/generation)
Natural Gas distribution (TX, MN, IN, OH)
revenue_streams.trend: stable/declining (Ohio divestiture closed Oct 2026, LA/MS sold Mar 2025)

business_model.customer_type: Regulated utility serving residential, commercial/industrial and transportation customers directly (gas) and indirectly via licensed Retail Electric Providers (electric, in deregulated ERCOT market); ~2.86 million metered electric customers in Houston, ~154k in Indiana, and ~4.0 million natural gas customers across four states
business_model.geographic_mix: Texas Gulf Coast/Houston (Electric + largest gas LDC), southwestern Indiana (Electric + gas, SIGECO), Minnesota (gas), Ohio (gas LDC sold Oct 1, 2026 for ~$2.62B)

competitive_position.market_position: Sole franchised transmission & distribution utility in its certificated Houston and southwestern Indiana service territories; one of the largest combined electric/gas utility holding companies in the U.S. by customer count

moat_factors.description: No competing electric T&D utility may legally operate in Houston Electric's or Indiana Electric's certificated territory without a new CCN/IURC certificate; Indiana service territory certificates are exclusive

moat_factors.factor: Rate base growth with regulatory cost recovery
moat_factors.description: ~85% of rate base has been through a rate case since 2023, and ~85% of projected capital investment is recoverable via interim trackers or forward-test-year rate cases, providing earnings visibility
Electricity and gas delivery are non-discretionary; demand is driven by weather, population and industrial growth rather than competitive dynamics
Operations spanning Texas, Indiana and Minnesota reduce single-regulator concentration, though Houston Electric remains the dominant earnings driver

weaknesses: Regulatory lag: capital spending outruns rate recovery between rate cases, pressuring near-term ROE
Houston Electric's receivables are concentrated in a small number of Retail Electric Providers (NRG and Vistra affiliates ~60% of billed receivables), creating counterparty risk
No generation ownership in Houston Electric (TEEEF leased units only) limits control over reliability during extreme events
High and rising leverage from the capital plan increases interest-rate and refinancing sensitivity
Legacy ZENS indexed debt security (tied to AT&T/Charter/WBD shares) is a persistent accounting/cash-flow complexity and tax risk

growth_drivers: 10-year, ~$70.7 billion capital investment plan (raised from $65B to $65.5B to $70.7B through 2026) driving rate-base and EPS growth

Forecast ~50% increase in Houston Electric peak load by 2029 (to 30+ GW) and nearly doubling by mid-2030s, driven by data centers, energy exports/refining, advanced manufacturing and logistics; ~14 GW of large-load interconnection requests submitted under ERCOT's Batch Zero process

Long-term guidance of 7%-9% annual non-GAAP EPS growth through 2030, with management now guiding to the mid-to-high end of that range, plus >$10 billion of additional, unguided capital opportunity identified through 2035
System resiliency plan (~$5.75 billion over 3 years) and post-Hurricane Beryl storm hardening investment, largely recoverable through securitization/trackers

Portfolio simplification via divestitures (Louisiana/Mississippi gas LDCs sold 2025; Ohio gas LDC sold October 2026 for ~$2.62B) to focus capital and management attention on core Texas/Indiana/Minnesota growth markets and fund the capital plan without excess equity dilution
Indiana Electric generation transition (coal retirements, wind/solar/storage additions) supporting rate base growth, tempered by customer-affordability-driven project cancellations

business.risk: Customer/counterparty concentration in Houston Electric REP receivables
business.description: ~37% and ~23% of billed receivables owed by NRG and Vistra affiliates respectively; REP financial distress or bankruptcy (as occurred after Feb 2021 Winter Storm) could impair collections

business.risk: TEEEF (temporary emergency generation) reliance and legislative/regulatory restriction
business.description: Houston Electric owns no generation; leased TEEEF units are being released/reduced under new Texas law, and recovery of ~$800M in TEEEF costs tied to Hurricane Beryl remains contested
Actual connection volume, timing and energization of the ~14 GW of large-load requests is uncertain and depends on ERCOT approval, construction and materials availability

financial.risk: High leverage / large external financing needs
financial.description: A $70.7B capital plan requires continuous debt and equity issuance (including forward equity sales); credit rating downgrades would raise borrowing costs and could restrict commercial paper access
Elevated rates increase interest expense (already up materially YoY) and pension obligation valuation, and tighten capital markets access for a capital-intensive business
Pre-2029 redemption or a wave of holder exchanges of the ZENS notes (tied to AT&T/Charter/WBD shares) could trigger significant cash tax payments and liquidity impacts

regulatory.description: Commissions may not approve full, timely recovery of capital plan costs or a reasonable ROE; customer affordability concerns already caused Indiana Electric to cancel ~$1 billion of renewable projects in 2025

regulatory.risk: Storm cost securitization and recovery proceedings
regulatory.description: Recovery of May 2024 storm and Hurricane Beryl costs required PUCT financing orders; future storms create recurring regulatory and securitization dependency
Repeal of the Endangerment Finding, OBBBA tax law changes and reversals of IRA energy credits create ongoing uncertainty for Indiana Electric's generation transition and tax planning (CAMT, PTCs)

macro.description: Houston Electric's entire service territory sits on the Texas Gulf Coast; Hurricane Beryl (2024) and the May 2024 storm events caused extensive damage, outages and litigation/regulatory scrutiny, and future hurricanes remain a recurring tail risk
Steel and equipment tariffs, skilled-labor shortages and supply disruptions raise capital plan execution costs and could cause delays or cost overruns
Rising customer bills from rate-base growth increase political and regulatory pushback risk during periods of high inflation or recession

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. regulated utility sector is in a multi-year capex supercycle driven by grid resiliency, electrification and AI/data-center-driven load growth; ERCOT (Texas) is forecasting among the fastest load growth of any U.S. grid
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low — regulated cost-of-service utility earnings are largely non-cyclical, though weather (especially in Texas, which lacks full weather-normalization mechanisms) and storm activity drive quarter-to-quarter variability
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — heavy reliance on debt and equity issuance to fund a ~$70.7B, 10-year capital plan makes financing costs and credit ratings central to the equity story
key_input_costs: Natural gas (pass-through via purchased gas adjustment)
Steel, transformers and grid equipment (capital plan materials)

Management reaffirmed and leaned toward the upper half of its long-standing 6-8%/7-9% long-term growth framework
Increased from ~$65.5B (Feb 2026) and $65B (Sep 2025); plus >$10 billion of additional unguided capital opportunities identified

items.target: ~85% of projected capital investment recoverable via interim trackers or forward-test-year rate cases
items.notes: Reduces regulatory lag risk on the large capital program

guidance.management_commentary: Management continues to frame CenterPoint as a pure-play, fully regulated utility concentrating on Electric and Natural Gas delivery, funding its capital plan through internally generated cash, debt issuance (including securitization bonds) and programmatic equity (ATM/forward sales) rather than large one-off equity raises, while citing data-center and industrial load growth in ERCOT as the primary long-term earnings driver and the Ohio divestiture as a further portfolio-simplification step.

bull_case: Rare combination of a fully regulated, monopoly-franchise utility with above-peer-average EPS growth guidance (7-9%, trending to the high end) underpinned by an escalating, near-$71B 10-year capital plan

Houston Electric sits at the epicenter of ERCOT's data-center/industrial load growth boom, with ~12 GW of large-load demand still active in the interconnection queue and peak load forecast to nearly double by the mid-2030s

Portfolio simplification (Ohio and Louisiana/Mississippi gas LDC sales) streamlines capital allocation toward the highest-growth Texas and Indiana jurisdictions and funds the capital plan with less equity dilution
Constructive regulatory mechanisms (trackers, forward test years, securitization of storm costs) cover ~85% of planned investment, limiting regulatory lag relative to peers
Consistent guidance raises in 2025-2026 (10-year plan increased three times; FY2026 EPS guidance raised at Q3) signal execution momentum and credibility with investors
bear_case: Heavy reliance on continuous debt and equity issuance to fund a ~$70.7B capital plan leaves CNP exposed to higher-for-longer interest rates, credit-rating pressure and dilution from ongoing forward equity sales

Houston Electric's Gulf Coast footprint carries recurring hurricane/severe-storm tail risk (Hurricane Beryl, May 2024 storms), with contested cost recovery (e.g., ~$800M TEEEF dispute) and litigation overhang

Realization of forecast data-center load growth is uncertain and could fall short of the ~14 GW originally requested given ERCOT interconnection queue attrition, construction delays and customer affordability pushback
Regulatory and political sensitivity to rising customer bills already forced cancellation of ~$1 billion of Indiana renewable projects in 2025, illustrating execution risk on the broader capital plan
Legacy complexity (ZENS indexed debt tied to AT&T/Charter/WBD share prices, pending Ohio divestiture true-ups) adds non-core financial and tax risk to an otherwise simple utility story
